masks.where: request heads, header values, bodies, frames, logs, env: the den port after `:`, `: ` or `RIVETOS_DEN_PORT=` (and the value of `RIVETOS_DEN_PORT` in env records)
masks.why: each den listens on a fresh free port; the harness substitutes the real port when it sends
per-run temp root (state dirs, HOME, roster, scripts, agent directories, the node symlink `{{TMP}}/bin/node`)
absolute path of the node binary running the den

masks.where: anywhere (`RIVET_DEN_NAME` is `<os.hostname()>:<roster key>`; it reaches session.start events and the child env)
anywhere: every `pty-<8 hex>` id (also inside `den-pty-<8 hex>` den sessions)
masks.why: ids come from crypto.randomBytes(4); numbered per den run in first-seen order. Request templates use the same tokens and the harness substitutes the live id

masks.where: the number after every `"pid":` (bodies, audit lines)
masks.why: child pids; numbered per den run in first-seen order

masks.where: any 13-digit number within 7 days of the harness start (createdAt, lastOutputTs, owner `since`, audit `ts`, event `ts`, session-cwd `at`)
masks.why: wall clock. Not numbered: two Date.now() reads in one synchronous block can straddle a millisecond, so equality between timestamps is not deterministic. Fixture timestamps (1760000000000) are never masked

conventions: request.head / request.body are templates: {{PORT}} and {{PTY_n}} are replaced by the live port and pty id when sent.
response.headers are [name, value] pairs in wire order and wire case; response.body is the exact payload after de-chunking (masked: bodyMasked true, bodyLength null).
log: den stdout/stderr lines emitted while the case or step ran.

WS frames: text frames verbatim (masked); binary frames as {text} when valid UTF-8 (masked) else {base64}. The first binary frame after a hello is the scrollback replay ({replay:true}); consecutive live output frames within one step are concatenated into one because PTY read chunking is timing-dependent (a comparator must concatenate the same way).
ping frames are not recorded: the den pings term clients from its 30 s heartbeat timer, so where one lands is timing; the harness still answers each with a pong.
sent: client frames the harness sent in the step (text, or binary as hex). sentClose: the harness sent a close frame with that code.

stateAfter: the den state dir (mode + masked text) after every PTY still running was killed one at a time by the harness (DELETE /term, wait for exit), or, for a run that ends in a recorded SIGTERM, just before that SIGTERM. agentDirs: the agents directory tree (preset directories created by ensureAgentDirectory).

steps.description: A types "hello\r" as a binary frame: tty echo + program line, mirrored to A and B.
A resize 120×40 with no owner: auto-claim → owner frames (self per recipient, since), log line, PTY resized (SIGWINCH → size:120x40).

stdout: term: owner none → another device for {{PTY_1}} (resize)

steps.description: B (not owner) resize 10×1000 → clamped 20×200 and only recorded: no frames, no resize.
B claims with no size: owner → B, B's recorded 20×200 applied.

stdout: term: owner another device → another device for {{PTY_1}} (claim)

steps.description: A claims with a size (float cols floored): owner → A, 81×25 applied.

stdout: term: owner another device → another device for {{PTY_1}} (claim)

steps.description: A claims again with the same size: owner unchanged (no frame, no log), applySize no-op.
Ignored control frames: not JSON, unknown type, array, resize with string/missing cols, null.
Binary frame 61 ff 62 0d: pty.ts:73 decodes per write (lossy) → the child reads 61 ef bf bd 62.
BUG (pty.ts:73): é (c3 a9) split across two binary frames becomes two U+FFFD; the child reads efbfbd efbfbd.
Same bytes in one frame arrive intact (c3a9).
A text frame that is valid JSON without a type is ignored (keystrokes are binary only).
B resizes (recorded, A owns), then A closes: B is the sole viewer → owner B (detach), B's 90×30 applied.

stdout: term: owner another device → another device for {{PTY_1}} (detach)
